paper: Al-Dayel et al., Scientific Reports (2025), DOI 10.1038/s41598-025-95511-y
scope: internal key-space arithmetic and key-material classification; not a cryptanalysis
arithmetic_observation: Each three-value component contributes 10^45 under the stated 10^15-per-value assumption; the text says 10^48, while its final product correctly uses 10^45.

key_material_audit.mapping_caveat: The paper does not clearly map these named secret parameters to the 56-value key-space enumeration; p,q,r,s are system parameters in Eq. 1 but omitted from the 8-value CDS count (they may be fixed public constants).
key_material_audit.classification: Data-derived/intermediate values are not automatically independent secret-key choices. Their contribution to effective secret entropy requires an explicit key-generation and adversary model.
key_material_audit.conditional_warning: 10^750 is only an illustrative upper-bound calculation assuming the other 50 values are independent secrets with 10^15 valid choices each; that assumption is not verified.

limitations: Decimal precision is not effective secret entropy.
The paper must distinguish independently chosen secret keys from plaintext-dependent, ciphertext-dependent, or intermediate values.
This audit establishes a mismatch in component arithmetic, not a weakness enabling key recovery.
